title: Industry status to Malayalam cinema: Single-window clearance for shooting, lower power tariffs for cinema halls among proposals mooted by film bodies
original_content: A special desk for single-window clearance for film shooting and other permissions from local bodies, relaxations in licensing norms for cinema halls and withdrawal of double taxation on movie tickets figure among the key recommendations submitted by the trade bodies in Malayalam cinema as part of the Keralam government’s decision to accord industry status to the sector. The government has forwarded the proposals made by various film bodies to the departments concerned, ahead of finalising the draft industry policy for Malayalam cinema. The final draft document will be placed before the Cabinet for approval soon, according to sources. The Kerala Film Chamber of Commerce (KFCC) has pushed for an end to the double taxation on movie tickets, among other proposals, submitted to the authorities. Anil Thomas, president of the KFCC, said the double taxation that included Goods and Services Tax (GST) and entertainment tax levied by local bodies had adversely affected the prospects of the industry for long. “We have also urged the government to relax certain licensing norms and to offer reduced electricity tariffs for cinema halls,” he said. The film bodies have pointed out the hassles in obtaining permissions for film shooting and recommended a separate cell to provide single-window clearance for such requests. B. Rakesh, president of Kerala Film Producers Association, said seeking permissions from multiple departments and bodies had often delayed film shooting process, resulting in increased production cost. “A single-window clearance will cut the bureaucratic delays. We have also urged the government to provide capital subsidy as part of extending the industry status to Malayalam cinema,” he said. Other recommendations Some of the other recommendations made by the film bodies include setting up a grievance cell to address workplace issues, easy access to tourist locations for shooting and improved access to bank loans at reduced interest rates based on the industry status. Minister for Culture P. C. Vishnunadh said the stakeholder consultations as part of granting industry status to Malayalam cinema have been positive. “The industry status will be granted before the October 9 deadline of the 100-day action plan of the United Democratic Front government,” he said. title: Keralam Forest dept begins operation to tranquillise, capture elephant ‘KM-1’ at Aralam
original_content: The Keralam Forest department has begun the operation to tranquillise and capture KM-1, the male elephant that entered the Aralam Rehabilitation Area, on Wednesday, with the animal being driven towards a designated 18-acre area. A prohibitory order has also been imposed in parts of Aralam, barring public gatherings during the operation. Division Forest Officer K. Saji said a team comprising 100 forest personnel had been deployed for the operation. The team includes a darting unit, two veterinarians, a conservation biologist and a supporting team, which has been fully deployed at the operation site and is prepared to undertake darting, if required, depending on the situation. As part of the operation, the driving team spotted KM-1 in the Block 10 Jalnidhi area of Aralam farm in the morning. Efforts are currently underway to drive it towards the designated 18-acre area. The tracking team had been operating in the Odachal area to locate and spot the elephant, where it had been staying. However, the presence of dense grassland in the vicinity of the elephant prevented the tracking team from approaching it directly. The tracking operation was temporarily halted for a short period in the afternoon and, following a tea break, the tracking team resumed efforts from the Kottappara-Pulinchod area to locate and spot the elephant. Meanwhile, as part of the operation to tranquillise and capture KM-1, District Collector P. Vishnuraj has imposed a prohibitory order under Section 163(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita in wards 6 and 7 of Aralam panchayat and Blocks 7, 9, 10 and 13 of Aralam farm. Under the order, members of the public are prohibited from assembling or gathering in these areas. Published - September 30, 2026 01:54 pm IST

title: Two Andhra Medical College PG students found dead within five days; probe on
original_content: Two postgraduate students of Andhra Medical College (AMC) in Visakhapatnam, one in her final year and the other in her first, have allegedly died by suicide within five days. The police are conducting a detailed inquiry into both deaths on the orders of Commissioner of Police Shankhabrata Bagchi. On September 24, P. Sailaja, a final-year postgraduate student in General Medicine, died at her residence under the III Town police station limits. Her family told the police that career-related stress could have been a factor. The III Town police registered a case and began an investigation. On September 28, Y. Sravani, a first-year ENT student from Hyderabad, died in her rented accommodation. She had not wanted to continue with the course, according to the police’s preliminary findings. A note left behind by her said that nobody should be held responsible for her death, the police said. The two incidents within a week have caused concern among the AMC student community and raised questions about the pressures faced by postgraduate medical students. If you are in distress, please reach out to Tele MANAS, the national mental health helpline, at 14416 or 1-800-891-4416. It is free and available round the clock. title: Telangana CM to inaugurate IDOC in Karimnagar, to lay foundation stones for ₹345.78 crore development works in Sircilla
original_content: Elaborate arrangements are in place for Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s visit to the erstwhile composite Karimnagar district on Wednesday, including his maiden visit to Sircilla as Chief Minister, where he will participate in development programmes and address a public meeting. Mr. Reddy will inaugurate the Integrated District Offices Complex (New Collectorate) in Karimnagar and review development initiatives with district officials. Issues including the Manair Riverfront Development Project, civic infrastructure and the dumping yard in Karimnagar are expected to figure in the meeting, sources said. Over 500 police personnel have been deployed for the bandobust arrangements in Karimnagar. In Sircilla, Mr. Reddy will lay foundation stones for development works worth around ₹345.78 crore, including expansion of the Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy temple complex and pilgrim amenities (Phase 1- Additional works) at Vemulawada at an estimated cost of ₹99.4 crore. He is also likely to take part in a padayatra before addressing a public meeting in the textile town of Sircilla. The public meeting assumes political significance as it marks Mr. Revanth Reddy’s maiden visit to Sircilla as Chief Minister. The constituency is represented by BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao. title: ‘Emotionally attached’ kin preserve Mumbai man’s body for 4 years after natural death: Police
original_content: The family of an 80-year-old Mumbai man who died four years ago has preserved his body due to “deep emotional attachment”, spending over ₹50 lakh in the process, police said on Wednesday (September 30, 2026). Ruling out any foul play, the police said the man passed away in 2022 after suffering from cancer, kidney failure, and other age-related ailments. The family initially kept the body in a freezer in their home in Mumbai’s Malad area, said an official from Kurar police station. According to the police, the man’s wife and two children, including a lawyer daughter, decided against performing the last rites due to “deep emotional attachment”. When their residential building went under redevelopment, the family moved the body to a local dispensary, which closed down about a month ago, they said. “The family has spent more than ₹50 lakh to keep the body preserved and was exploring options to send it to a facility in the United States offering long-term cryopreservation services,” a police official said. Cryopreservation broadly refers to storing cells, tissues or organs at extremely low temperatures. The unusual case came to light after cops received a tip-off. Relatives and neighbours were aware of the arrangement, and police ruled out anything suspicious, saying the death was natural. No case has been registered in the matter, and the family is currently deciding whether to proceed with sending the body abroad or perform the last rites, the official added. Published - September 30, 2026 02:09 pm IST

title: ED arrests Vatika Group CMD, promoter in PMLA case
original_content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested Vatika Limited chairman-cum-managing director Anil Bhalla and promoter Gautam Bhalla in an alleged money-laundering case linked to allegations of fraudulent inducement and non-delivery of residential plots. The ED case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) is based on multiple First Information Reports registered by the Economic Offences Wing of the Delhi police. Between 2010 and 2012, seven purchaser entities paid ₹260 crore upfront to Vatika Limited as the entire sale consideration for residential plots in its Vatika India Next projects in Sectors 84/85 and Vatika India Next-2 in Sector 88A, Gurugram. Plot-wise agreements were subsequently executed in 2014 and 2015, the agency said. Thereafter, the project layouts were revised, the plots originally allotted were renumbered or relocated, and the project land continued to be allotted and sold to different buyers. The ED alleged that in Vatika India Next-2, not a single plot out of about 1.10 lakh sq. yd. purchased for about ₹90 crore had been delivered even after nearly 14 years, while delivery in Vatika India Next had been only partial. As a result, plots worth about ₹140.73 crore remained undelivered, it said. According to the ED, the project land was held through around 22 group companies which had no employees or separate business activities and were mainly used to provide corporate guarantees and manage the land bank, including its mortgage to financial institutions. The agency examined the bank accounts of Vatika Limited and found that the money received from buyers was not used exclusively for the projects. Instead, the funds were transferred to other group companies and promoter-linked entities that were not part of these projects, it alleged. In 2024, Scaler Ventures paid ₹473.18 crore under an Agreement to Sell and a Buy-Back Agreement. The ED alleged that only 15 of the 165 plots were bought back. Thereafter, 14 of the remaining 150 plots were allegedly sold to third parties for about ₹13.62 crore without Scaler’s knowledge or consent, alleged the ED. Published - September 30, 2026 02:32 pm IST

title: 'Pilot Stabbed': What Happened Inside flydubai Flight Before 'Hijack' Signal
original_content: A commercial plane travelling from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Israel was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after briefly transmitting emergency codes, including one associated with a possible hijacking. The flydubai plane transmitted an emergency alert shortly after takeoff, prompting Israel to scramble warplanes, according to publicly available flight tracking information. However, Israeli media, citing security officials, later reported that the incident stemmed from a feud between the plane's two pilots, and everyone on board was safe. The plane landed in Tabuk, a civilian and military base in Saudi Arabia. The Incident Flight-tracking data showed that the Boeing 737 MAX 8, operating as flight FZ1073 from Dubai International Airport to Ben Gurion Airport, first transmitted squawk code 7700, the internationally recognised code for a general emergency. However, the flight soon switched the code to 7500, which indicates unlawful interference with an aircraft, including a possible hijacking. The signal, though, alone does not establish what happened aboard the flight, which had about 180 Israeli passengers on board. The Clash Of Pilots Later, citing security officials, The Jerusalem Post reported that the plane was forced to make an emergency landing after a "violent" altercation between two pilots. According to the report, everyone on board was safe. A regional official briefed on the incident told the Associated Press that a fight broke out in the cockpit and apparently involved pilots. It wasn't immediately clear what had caused the fight, the official said. The pilots reportedly activated the hijack code while fighting. Another report claimed the pilot tried to commit suicide and crash the plane with him. Citing passengers on board the flight, the Times of Israel reported that one of the pilots stabbed another. Some Israeli passengers reportedly helped the crew to subdue the attacker. Another passenger on the flight, Miriam, told Channel 15 that passengers heard shouting during the flight. When the cockpit door was opened, there was blood inside. According to her, one of the pilots was struck with a folding knife. The passengers, together with the crew, intervened in the fight and stopped it. After that, the plane made an emergency landing. Miriam said that at one point the passengers thought they would not make it out alive. The Flight Dropped 17,000 Ft According to a CNN report, the emergency signal was issued after the aircraft dropped 17,400 feet in altitude, from 34,000 to around 16,600 feet, over just two minutes at around 1:20 am Eastern Time. The first emergency signal was sent from the aircraft at 1:32 am ET. A second official said that Israel had scrambled warplanes, fearing a hijacking of a plane carrying dozens of its citizens. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned recently of unspecified, escalated security threats. "Following concerns over an aviation incident, Prime Minister Netanyahu held consultations on the matter and is monitoring developments. The incident is under control, and all measures are currently being deployed in order to return the Israeli passengers safely to Israel," Netanyahu's office said about the incident. Israel has not experienced a hijacking in decades but maintains some of the strictest airport security in the world. Commercial flights have been operating between Israel and the United Arab Emirates since the two countries normalised their ties in 2020. title: CMRL-Exalogic payoff case: Kerala HC reserves order on plea seeking FIR against Pinarayi, daughter Veena, Riyas
original_content: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) reserved its verdict in a petition seeking the registration of an FIR and investigation by the State Police Chief into the predicate offence found during an Enforcement Directorate (ED) probe in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. Justice A. Badharudeen reviewed the information passed by the ED to the State Police Chief and observed orally that the question of whether to conduct a preliminary inquiry before registering an FIR would have to be analysed on “a case-to-case basis.” The court stated that the general principle was that a report or information provided by the ED under the Prevention of Corruption Act (PCA) was “a substitute” for preliminary inquiry, which is usually used to find if there was any truth in the allegations. The court further enquired why the ED had not challenged the State police’s inaction in registering an FIR. It further inquired whether the case diary was the sole evidence submitted and if witness statements had been furnished. ED response The ED responded that the statements would also be produced if required. Previously, the ED had explained in court that, while investigating the offences under the PMLA Act allegedly committed by T. Veena, daughter of Keralam Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan and her now-defunct company Exalogic, the agency received information regarding a predicate offence, which would fall under the purview of the State police. Accordingly, the ED shared the information with the State Police Chief. Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala had recently said an FIR could not be lodged against Mr. Vijayan, Ms. Veena and her husband P.A. Mohamed Riyas merely based on a proposal from the ED in the case. Mr. Chennithala said the State was not opposed to registering an FIR in the case. However, a preliminary inquiry would be conducted first based on the Advocate General’s advice, as “certain things needed further clarity.” The petitioner, lawyer K.M. Shajahan, had reportedly approached the State Police Chief and the Director of Vigilance earlier, seeking registration of an FIR and investigation into allegations of disproportionate assets, intentional enrichment of Mr. Vijayan and abetment under the PCA and alleged money laundering by Ms. Veena and Mr. Riyas. Published - September 30, 2026 02:32 pm IST

Justice A. Badharudeen reviewed ED information and questioned why they had not challenged police inaction. The court asked if witness statements were provided, to which the ED responded that more evidence would be produced if needed. Meanwhile, Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala stated an FIR could not be registered without a preliminary inquiry based on Advocate General’s advice. Published September 30, 2026.

title: LPU protest: High Court seeks status report from Punjab govt.
original_content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) sought a status report from the Punjab government on a probe into the violence and vandalism that erupted at Lovely Professional University in Phagwara days ago. The matter came up for hearing before the bench headed by Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra in the High Court on a plea by Lovely Professional University (LPU) BTech student, Ravi Raj, seeking a CBI probe into the vandalism and violence at LPU. Speaking to the media after the hearing, Additional Solicitor Advocate General Satyapal Jain said the High Court has sought a status report on the Punjab Police's investigation. "A complete status report (has been sought), what action has been taken, who are the culprits, what action has been taken against them, what action is being taken," he said. The next hearing is on October 8. Mr. Jain said it was important to identify those behind spreading the misleading information on campus, as he expressed apprehension that a planned conspiracy appears to be behind it. Mr. Raj, the petitioner, submitted that an unverified post was circulated among the students on the night of September 26 claiming that a female student had been raped on the campus and sent home. Students gathered outside the girls' hostel and later blocked National Highway-44, according to the plea. Later, a large number of outsiders, carrying swords, rods and sickles with their faces covered, reached the LPU campus and broke open the varsity main gates, destroyed CCTV cameras, looted shops and set several places on fire. In the petition, the LPU student submitted that the relevant rules of the IT Act should have been enforced when the misleading rumours spread on the campus. LPU students held a massive protest on Sunday. Also, they blocked a stretch of the New Delhi-Amritsar Highway outside their campus over claims that an outsider had raped a female student on the university premises. Violence also broke out on the campus, with students saying that some outsiders with their faces covered indulged in vandalism, damaged property, ransacked shops and also set several places on fire on the LPU campus. Normalcy returned to the LPU campus on Monday (September 28, 2026), with many students heading home after classes were suspended for 10 days. Published - September 30, 2026 02:33 pm IST

title: Opinion | Why Does Trump Want To Sell Arms To A US 'Adversary'? Inside His Strange Bargain
original_content: Opinion | Why Does Trump Want To Sell Arms To A US 'Adversary'? Inside His Strange Bargain Trump's aides maintain that no such offer had been made. But the story points to a larger strategy The Trump administration's handling of Taiwan arms sales points to a broader shift in the way Washington is managing its China policy. A roughly USD 14 billion package for Taiwan, primarily air-defence systems, missiles and counter-drone capabilities, has reportedly been kept in abeyance, with Trump describing it as a “very good negotiating chip” with Beijing. The message is unmistakable: Taiwan's security assistance is no longer being treated simply as an element of US deterrence policy, but also as an instrument in the wider US-China bargain. That approach may offer Washington tactical leverage. But it also creates strategic uncertainty for Taiwan and, more importantly, for US allies and partners across the Indo-Pacific. Taiwan As An Instrument Congress advanced the roughly USD 14 billion package earlier in 2026, but Trump has yet to give final approval. Following his May summit with Xi Jinping in Beijing, he said the package was being held “in abeyance” and that its fate “depends on China.” He also acknowledged that Taiwan arms sales had been discussed with Xi in considerable detail. This is significant because it moves beyond the traditional logic of US arms transfers to Taiwan. The Six Assurances, alongside the Taiwan Relations Act, have long provided the framework within which Washington has maintained Taiwan's defensive capacity while avoiding an explicit commitment to Taiwanese independence. Consulting Beijing over the timing or substance of arms deliveries risks giving China a degree of influence over a policy that Washington has historically sought to keep within its own strategic calculus. The administration has offered more than one explanation for the delay, including the desire to retain leverage with Beijing and pressure on US munitions stocks because of military operations involving Iran. These explanations need not be mutually exclusive. But from the perspective of allies, the important issue is not merely why a particular package is delayed. It is whether future security commitments can similarly become contingent on unrelated negotiations with Beijing. A previous package of roughly $11 billion was approved in late 2025, underscoring that the administration has not abandoned arms transfers to Taiwan. The question, therefore, is less about an immediate rupture in policy than about the emerging pattern of conditionality. The China Arms-Sale Episode The reported remarks by US Ambassador to China David Perdue add another layer of uncertainty. Last week, following Xi's state visit to Washington, Perdue said on Fox News that Trump had at one point asked Xi whether China would like to buy US weapons, arguing that Washington sells arms to countries around the world. The White House and State Department quickly rejected the suggestion that there was an actual offer or plan to sell weapons to China, pointing to US law prohibiting such sales. Trump himself disputed Perdue's characterisation, suggesting that the ambassador may have been referring to Taiwan and saying that China would probably prefer superior American equipment, while adding that such a sale had not been discussed. The episode is therefore best understood as a contested account rather than evidence of an actual US plan to arm China. Yet the fact that the remark required such rapid clarification is itself revealing. Strategic signalling is not simply about what governments intend; it is also about what allies and adversaries believe Washington is prepared to contemplate. The Alliance Problem For US allies, Taiwan is not an isolated issue. Japan, Australia, the Philippines and South Korea all have an interest in the credibility of American deterrence in the western Pacific. A conflict over Taiwan would have consequences for regional sea lanes, military deployments, supply chains and the broader balance of power. This makes the handling of Taiwan arms sales a test of alliance confidence. If Washington can temporarily suspend a major Taiwanese arms package to gain leverage with Beijing, allies will inevitably consider what this means for their own security relationships with the United States. The concern is not necessarily that Washington will abandon Taiwan. Rather, it is that security commitments could become increasingly transactional, with their implementation conditioned by the demands of a larger US-China bargain. That perception could encourage greater hedging. Japan and Australia may accelerate indigenous defence capabilities; Southeast Asian partners may diversify security relationships; and governments across the region may become more cautious about aligning themselves too closely with Washington during periods of intensified US-China competition. The practical consequences are also important. Taiwan already faces long delivery timelines for many American systems. Additional delays thus have effects beyond the immediate political signal. They complicate defence planning and force modernisation and the sequencing of military capabilities. The wider US problem of competing munitions demands, from Europe and the Middle East to the Indo-Pacific, only reinforces these pressures. Beijing's Opportunity For China, the episode offers both a diplomatic and informational advantage. Beijing has consistently opposed American arms sales to Taiwan, which it regards as part of its territory, and has sought to constrain or delay such transfers. If Chinese objections can contribute to postponing US weapons deliveries, Beijing gains something more consequential than a single policy concession: evidence that diplomatic engagement with Washington can influence the operational tempo of American support for Taiwan. Chinese state media has already used Trump's comments to question the reliability of American backing for Taipei. Such narratives serve Beijing's broader objective of persuading Taiwan that dependence on the United States carries risks, and that accommodation with China may ultimately be unavoidable. The strategic question, therefore, is whether Beijing is being given a de facto role in determining the timing of US military assistance to Taiwan. That would represent a significant shift in the regional balance of signalling. The Larger Dilemma The central tension is between transactional diplomacy and strategic consistency. Trump's approach places a premium on using every available instrument-trade, agriculture, aircraft purchases, military sales and diplomatic engagement - to shape Chinese behaviour. From that perspective, delaying Taiwan arms sales can be presented as pragmatic statecraft rather than abandonment. But deterrence depends not only on capabilities; it depends on expectations. Allies and adversaries must have some confidence that commitments will survive changes in the diplomatic weather. If weapons deliveries to Taiwan become another variable in summit negotiations with Xi, the United States risks creating uncertainty precisely where deterrence requires clarity. The distinction between a temporary delay and an indefinite freeze is thus crucial. A short postponement linked to logistics, stockpile management or immediate diplomatic circumstances is one thing. A prolonged delay explicitly conditioned on Beijing's satisfaction would send a very different signal. For Washington's partners, the issue is consequently larger than the USD 14 billion package itself. They will be watching whether the package, or a modified version of it, eventually moves forward, whether the administration continues to reaffirm the Taiwan Relations Act and Six Assurances, and whether future US-China summits produce similar conditionality. The reported discussion about possible US arms sales to China, even after being denied and disputed, adds to the uncertainty. At a time when the Indo-Pacific is already adjusting to a more contested balance of power, Washington's challenge is not simply to negotiate effectively with Beijing. It is to ensure that the pursuit of a better US-China relationship does not generate doubts among the very partners whose confidence underpins American strategy in Asia. This move shifts the traditional US policy on Taiwan's security and raises concerns among allies about the transactional nature of future security commitments. title: Keralam bypoll results a strong indicator that CPI(M) has not lost its ground: A. Vijayaraghavan
original_content: Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] Polit Bureau member A. Vijayaraghavan has said that the outcome of the by-elections held in Keralam has proved that the Left front “cannot be uprooted from the hearts of the public.” The electorate has responded against the United Democratic Front (UDF) government at the first opportunity after it came to power, he said in his inaugural address at the extended Ernakulam District Committee meeting of the CPI(M) in Kochi on Wednesday to discuss the party’s electoral setback in the 2026 Assembly elections. Mr. Vijayaraghavan said the bypoll results had come as a befitting reply to the campaign that the CPI(M) had lost its ground. “Our opponents will now accelerate their efforts to weaken it and we have to resist such attempts,” he said. He accused Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan of not yet coming clear on who had sponsored his recent chartered flight to Malappuram. The government needed to carry out an introspection as such trips lacked transparency, he alleged. On the recent foreign trips of a few Ministers in the UDF government, Mr. Vijayaraghavan said they needed to be aware that they were bound by protocol while making such trips abroad. They needed to check the credentials of those offering them hospitality abroad. The CPI(M) had regulated the foreign trips of its Ministers in the first few years after it came to power, he claimed. Mr. Vijayaraghavan said the party would conduct a serious scrutiny of the reasons behind its defeat in the Assembly polls and initiate the required course correction. Published - September 30, 2026 02:53 pm IST

Vijayaraghavan**, a **Communist Party of India (Marxist)** Polit Bureau member, stated at an Ernakulam District Committee meeting in Kochi that the Left front's recent by-election victories proved its enduring support despite electoral setbacks in 2026 Assembly elections. title: Indian Among 5 Crew Members Killed On Hijacked Tanker Off Somalia Coast
original_content: An Indian sailor was among five crew members killed by pirates aboard a hijacked fuel tanker in Somalia, authorities said, as security forces of the African nation retook control of the vessel. The Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) said three Pakistanis, one Indian and one Myanmar national were killed early on Tuesday, before its forces launched an operation to secure the Palau-flagged tanker MT Honour 25, news portal Somalia Today reported. Three Pakistani crew members and one Indian national were also wounded, it said. Puntland is a semi-autonomous state of Somalia. PMPF blamed the deaths on the Somali pirates holding the vessel off the coast of Puntland but did not provide details on how or when the crew members were killed. According to the European Union's naval force EUNAVFOR, the vessel was hijacked in April while travelling towards Somalian capital, Mogadishu. It was carrying about 17 crew members, most of them Pakistani nationals, and a cargo of oil products. title: A farmer left $10.9 million to build a cancer centre; Mayo Clinic was supposed to get it only if the local hospital lost its independence
original_content: Iowa farmer Herman Carl Stille died in September 2020 at 94, leaving an estate worth about $10.9 million. His 2017 will directed the remainder to Floyd County Medical Center (FCMC) in Charles City to establish a cancer centre for local residents. It also named the Mayo Foundation as the alternative recipient, for Alzheimer's research, if the hospital lost its independence and became part of a major healthcare corporation. Mayo went to court after the hospital found it could not provide radiation treatment. On May 1, 2026, the Iowa Supreme Court ruled in favour of the medical centre. A farmer's $10.9 million will with two conditions Stille was a cattle farmer and factory worker before he retired. He never married, had no children and left no living siblings or other identified heirs. He received care at FCMC for more than a decade and was the largest donor to the hospital's charitable foundation. He was also a Mayo patient in Rochester, Minnesota, and had given to its charitable foundation. His last gift there came in January 2017. He stopped donating because he was dissatisfied with the care he received, and his later gifts went to FCMC alone. The $10.9 million estate was mostly farmland. After several small charitable bequests, his will, signed in August 2017, gave the remainder to the hospital for a cancer centre. It required an oncologist on staff, office and consultation space, a family area and separate areas for radiation, chemotherapy and other treatments. The gift was contingent on the hospital staying independent. If it lost its independent status and joined a major healthcare corporation, the remainder would go to Mayo Foundation for Alzheimer's research. Attorney Michael Kennedy, who drafted the will, testified that Stille added the independence requirement in 2017. Stille's earlier will, from 2011, had no such condition and named Mayo as the backup only if the cancer centre could not be established. Stille's sister had died from Alzheimer's complications, and he feared facing the same disease. Radiation proved impossible After Stille's death, FCMC began planning the centre, expecting roughly $10 million from the estate. Administrators soon realised they could not provide on-site radiation. Radiation requires a linear accelerator, which is costly and heavily regulated. In Iowa, a hospital needs a certificate of need, and one is generally not issued when radiation facilities already operate within a certain radius. Several hospitals near FCMC already offered radiation. The machine is also expensive to run, and FCMC lacked the patient base to afford its upkeep. The hospital said the centre could still satisfy the other requirements. It proposed to staff an oncologist through cooperation or subcontracting with other facilities, and to transport patients to another facility for radiation. It also noted that more cancer patients are treated with chemotherapy than with radiation. Mayo's challenge Mayo asked the court to rule that the gift to FCMC had failed. It argued that the will's conditions went beyond independence, and that the money should pass to it if FCMC could not build the centre Stille described. Kennedy testified that Stille's intent was for the money to go to Mayo if either condition was unmet. FCMC countered that it had remained independent, so the trigger for Mayo's gift had never occurred. The Chickasaw County district court, after a three-day bench trial, ruled for FCMC in June 2025. It found that the hospital was independent and that its planned centre would meet five of the six specifications, all but radiation. The judge concluded that Stille cared more about the hospital's independence than about how the centre would operate, and would not have withdrawn the bequest had he known radiation was impossible. Iowa Supreme Court affirms on standing Mayo appealed, and the Supreme Court retained the case. On May 1, 2026, it unanimously affirmed, in an opinion by Justice Thomas Waterman. Justice Mansfield took no part. The court did not adopt the district court's reasoning. It found no ambiguity in the will, which conditioned the gift to Mayo on FCMC's loss of independence. Because FCMC remained independent, and Mayo did not dispute that, the court held that Mayo takes nothing under the will. A beneficiary whose condition has not occurred lacks standing to challenge the gift to someone else, so the court affirmed on that basis alone and did not reach the remaining issues. The court noted that FCMC still has a legal and moral obligation to use the funds as intended. Mayo cannot enforce it, but the Iowa attorney general has standing to enforce the terms of charitable trusts. The ruling ends a dispute that began in 2021 and leaves the remainder of the $10.9 million estate with FCMC. The hospital says it will proceed with the Stille Cancer Centre on its campus. It says it is still unclear which cancer services will be available, including how radiation care will be provided for patients who need it.

If FCMC could not meet these requirements, the Mayo Foundation was named as an alternative recipient for Alzheimer's research. In May 2026, the Iowa Supreme Court ruled in favor of FCMC after Mayo contested the will due to FCMC’s inability to provide on-site radiation treatment. The court upheld that FCMC remained independent and thus eligible for the full bequest.

title: Gandak floods Bihar’s West Champaran as three embankments breach, creates panic among residents
original_content: After heavy rains in catchment areas in Nepal, flood in Gandak river, known as Narayani in Nepal, breached at least three embankments in last two-days in West Champaran district of Bihar on Indo-Nepal border and created panic among residents. The breaches from Monday (September 28, 2026) night to Tuesday (September 29, 2026) morning inundated low-lying areas and agricultural fields, and also flooded Bagaha town area. The Gandak, Kosi, Bagmati, and Sone rivers are in spate, with rising water levels posing a threat to Bihar’s border districts. Following the heavy discharge of water from the Valmikinagar barrage along the border area, the first breach occurred at Kharatwa Daroga Chowk under Singhari Pipariya panchayat in Bagaha on September 28 night, while the second breach was reported near Phulia Khad village in Bairia block. The third embankment breach occurred on September 29 morning near Makari Tesarahiya village leading to floodwaters gushing into nearly half a dozen surrounding villages like Chakhani, Rjwatia, Pipariya, Bargaon, Belwa, Dumaria, Patilar, Ratwal, Lgunaha and others. A record 5.43 lakh cusecs of water was discharged from Valmikinagar barrage on September 28. Several eports noted that a ring bandha (embankment) near Pandey Tola in Shreya Panchayat of Areraj Block in East Champaran district was breached in the wee hours of September 30. However, officials have not confirmed it yet. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has been conducting aerial surveys of the affected areas and giving instructions to the top district official for speedy relief and rescue measures. In the affected areas of West Champaran district, affected families have taken shelter on elevated spaces of the embankments. There are also reports of villagers themselves breaching embankments to allow floodwaters to spread over a larger area to minimize intensity of the damage. The district administration has launched a day-night patrolling on the embankments in the district to prevent further breach. Principal Secretary of the State Disaster Management Department (DMD) Santosh Kumar Mall said one company each of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) had been dispatched to the affected areas. “Besides, two companies of NDRF and SDRF are already stationed in the Champaran districts to meet any eventuality”, he said. DMD officials said the water levels in the swollen rivers has shown declining trend, bringing relief to the residents. “The administration of adjoining districts has also been put on high alert following the surge in river waters”, an official said. Relief camps have been set up in the affected areas, including one at a high school in Bathana village of Bairiya block. “As many as 23 community kitchens are running in all across West Champaran district,” said Taranjot Singh, the District Magistrate, adding that water levels have started receding in parts of Bagaha subdivision, where floodwaters had entered even the town areas. Meanwhile, residents of affected villages were seen running from one elevated location to another, carrying their belongings and livestock. Black colour tarpaulin sheets have been distributed among them by the district administration. “Destiny has played a cruel joke on us by flooding our villages and home”, said Sanjay Dubey, a resident of Bagaha who was taking shelter on an embankment. Earlier, the Ganga and several of its tributaries had also swollen, flooding areas like Punpun and Hatidah in Patna district. Subsequently, the waters receded without any major casualties. However, with heavy rainfall continuing in the catchment areas of neighboring Nepal, Bihar’s border districts are once again facing a flood threat as rivers swell across the region. Embankments in Gopalganj and Saran districts too have breached at some places. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary conducted another aerial survey of the flood affected areas of Champaran on Wednesday (September 30, 2026). Published - September 30, 2026 02:54 pm IST

The Valmikinagar barrage discharged a record 5.43 lakh cusecs of water on September 28. Floodwaters inundated Bagaha town and several villages, prompting residents to seek shelter on embankments. Relief camps were set up, with community kitchens providing food. title: In Flood-Hit Nepal, Teachers Mourn Students Who Never Returned
original_content: Each morning at a school in flood-ravaged Nepal, teachers taking attendance are served a painful reminder of the disaster as they mark in red the names of students who never came back. The catastrophic flood, triggered by a glacial collapse near the China-Nepal border, killed more than 1,400 people, the majority in Nepal. Over 5,000 remain missing in the Himalayan nation one month after the tsunami-like waves swept away roads, bridges and settlements in the mountainous regions up north. At the Neelakantha Secondary School in hard-hit Rasuwa district, a teacher marked red circles beside the names of children missing since the August 26 flood. Unlike more than a dozen schools destroyed by the floods, the Neelakantha school, sitting on relatively higher ground, remained largely intact. But it lost 70 of its students and four teachers. "If you look at Rasuwa, you can't find a family that has not lost a family member," principal Madhav Lamichhane told AFP. "All the students and teachers are going through the same pain." Most of the missing Neelakantha pupils were on their way to the school from riverside settlements when floodwaters tore through the valley. "We have been remembering our students with every breath," said Rama Paudel, a 36-year-old teacher. "They have lost their lives in this disaster at such a young age. It's a great loss." Across Rasuwa and neighbouring districts, around 500 students and 24 teachers remain missing, while 18 schools have been damaged, with recovery costs estimated at up to $15.47 million, according to government data. "This is the worst situation ever the education sector has experienced," education ministry spokesman Shree Prasad Bhattarai told AFP. 'Feel normal again' Initial assessments by UNICEF show learning has been disrupted for more than 14,000 children at 62 schools and learning centres across the flood-affected region. "Education is a critical part of children's recovery after a disaster," UNICEF representative Alice Akunga said last week. "Returning to learning provides children with a sense of stability, routine and hope at a time when many have experienced significant loss and uncertainty." For many families, however, sending children back to school was not yet possible. Fewer than half of Neelakantha Secondary School's 508 students have resumed classes since lessons restarted two weeks ago. Principal Lamichhane said around 150 students were still unable to reach the school because bridges and roads had been swept away. Some classrooms have been repurposed as relief distribution centres, underscoring the challenges of restoring normalcy. Teachers say psychological scars may prove even harder to overcome than damaged infrastructure. "We have many students who do not have their parents or have seen their friends being swept away," said teacher Shiva Ram Bhatta. "It has been a month now, but it is difficult for them to focus." Relief supplies are reaching many survivors, he said, but the next phase of recovery will require much more than food and shelter. "We have enough relief materials," he said. "Now we need psychosocial therapy and a permanent way out so that they can feel normal again." title: Cornell University gang-rape case: DA reveals new disturbing details as investigation reopens
original_content: The district attorney (DA) who has reopened his investigation into an alleged 2024 sexual assault at Cornell University has defended his earlier decision not to prosecute anyone, citing the former student’s own account of the incident to police. Also Read | Drugged with ketamine, raped for hours: Ex-student sues Cornell University, 7 fraternity members In several media interviews on Tuesday (local time), Tompkins County DA Matthew Van Houten argued that while the male students involved did things that were “morally wrong”, the woman’s initial account of the incident to police did not include allegations that she was drugged, incapacitated beyond the ability to consent, or forced to engage in sexual activity. “She went to the police because she knew it wasn’t right,” Van Houten told CNN. “There were no question marks. There was no additional need to find information because we had all of the information that the police collected from Jane Doe through her very detailed, very comprehensive statement that she provided,” he added. Van Houten has not released the complainant’s sworn statement to police, but instead made public a summary that includes some of her direct quotes. He also defended his office’s decision not to conduct further investigation after the woman, identified in court filings by the pseudonym "Jane Doe," initially spoke to police. The woman filed a lawsuit this month alleging that she was assaulted by seven male students at the Chi Phi fraternity house on Cornell’s campus in October 2024. According to the lawsuit, the alleged incident occurred after she was pressured into taking drugs and consuming alcohol, leaving her unable to consent to sexual activity. The complainant reported the incident to Cornell’s campus police, but Van Houten’s office decided not to prosecute anyone at the time. The office later reopened the criminal investigation amid growing public attention over the woman’s allegations. Cornell supports reopening investigation Cornell University has expressed support for reopening the criminal investigation, saying in a statement that its own inquiry had resulted in disciplinary action against some students, including expulsions. According to the statement, the Chi Phi chapter remains barred from campus. The woman’s lawsuit accuses the university of failing to prevent the alleged assaults and of not adequately addressing sexual violence on campus. It includes a photograph that purportedly shows a group chat between fraternity members discussing the events of that night. Van Houten dismissed the photograph as a “red herring”, arguing that it had no bearing on the legal assessment of whether the woman had consented or whether there was evidence that she had been unable to consent under state law. “We received it, but it was not relevant to the assessment of whether Jane Doe consented or whether there was any evidence of lack of consent on her part as defined by the penal law,” he said. (With AP inputs)

title: Congress pursues politics of “divide Hindus for Muslim rule”: BJP
original_content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) accused the Congress and Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy of seeking to divide Hindu society along regional, linguistic, caste, and gender lines, while referring to Mr. Reddy’s remarks on Lord Shiva and Lord Rama. title: In 2019, Chip and Joanna Gaines bought Waco’s neglected Cottonland Castle; after years restoring the 6,176-sq-ft landmark, the ‘Fixer Upper’ property listed for $2.7 million has found a buyer
original_content: For years, Cottonland Castle stood as one of Waco's most intriguing landmarks, an imposing historic home that had plenty of character but needed someone willing to take on the work. In 2019, that someone was Chip and Joanna Gaines. After years spent restoring and reimagining the property, the famous Waco couple's castle has now found a buyer, states an online report by PEOPLE. The Historic Waco Castle, also known as Cottonland Castle, went pending on Sept. 18 after being listed for $2.7 million in June. The eventual sale price has not been disclosed. The Gaineses had previously explored selling the property through an auction in 2023, adds the online report. A 135-year-old Waco landmark As per PEOPLE, the castle dates back roughly 135 years and occupies 6,176 square feet. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom residence combines the imposing character of a historic structure with the highly considered interiors associated with the Gaineses' Magnolia brand. Its restoration focused on preserving the property's historic identity while making the house functional as a modern home. Antique tile floors, diamond-paned windows and other period details remain central to the design, adds the report. Inside, the layout includes a formal dining room and a spacious great room, along with more distinctive spaces such as a card room, library and conservatory. Together, the rooms give the house a character that is unusual even among historic Texas properties, the online report elaborates. From neglected property to TV project The castle's transformation became a television project when the Gaineses documented the renovation for their 2022 Magnolia Network series Fixer Upper: The Castle. The show followed the couple as they tackled the challenges of bringing the aging structure back to life. For Chip Gaines, the property had long been a personal ambition. He had reportedly followed the castle for years, making repeated attempts to acquire it whenever it returned to the market. The restoration ultimately became one of the couple's most ambitious projects, combining architectural preservation with the layered design approach that has become synonymous with Fixer Upper. The latest property move The castle is not the only Waco property the Gaineses have been dealing with this year. Around the same time Cottonland Castle was listed, the couple also put their Colonial-style Hillcrest Estate on the market for $1.7 million. The five-bedroom, four-bathroom property had previously been offered as a short-term rental through Airbnb and the Magnolia website. It remains listed for sale, according to property records. The Gaineses have also taken on another notable restoration project involving an abandoned factory building that was transformed into the Gristmill. The property, which viewers may recognize from Joanna Gaines' Magnolia Table cooking show, was listed for $935,000 and remains on the market. A new chapter for the castle The pending sale marks the latest chapter in Cottonland Castle's long history. What began as a neglected historic property became a high-profile restoration project and a television centerpiece before returning to the real estate market. title: J&K to draft guidelines regulating social media journalists
original_content: The Jammu and Kashmir government is working on a new media policy to regulate the mushrooming of social media journalists, the Legislative Assembly was informed on Wednesday (September 30, 2026). Responding to a question from National Conference (NC) MLA Bashir Veeri, Minister Sakina Itoo said the Assembly’s House Committee, constituted to examine the matter, has given the Information Department four months to formulate new guidelines. Ms. Itoo said the House Committee, headed by senior MLA and former minister Ali Mohammad Sagar, met on July 13, 2026. Several members raised concerns over the mushrooming growth of social media journalists and demanded strict guidelines. Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather said he had asked the government during the Budget Session to conduct a comprehensive study of media functioning and formulate guidelines for taking action against those who violate the law. Mr. Veeri’s colleague, NC MLA Nazir Gurezi, said anyone can pick up a phone and become a journalist these days. “Then social media is being misused. There should be some regulation,” he demanded. Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) MLA Waheed Para said, “We are living in the 21st century, and demanding censorship is not the right thing.” Ms. Itoo said the issue concerns the House. “A half-hour discussion was held in the Budget Session, and the government gave its reply at that time. Without the media — whether print or electronic — we are incomplete; there is no two ways about it. But, Sir, there are certain shortcomings now; there is no doubt about that either,” she said. Ms. Itoo said in this era of mobile phones, legislators also share the blame. “We keep our close associates around to photograph everything here so that the pictures can be published outside later. We cannot place the entire blame on media personnel alone,” she said. She informed the Assembly that a member has opened a social media page under the name of his wife’s maid. “There are some honourable members — I will not take names — an honourable member has created a page under the name of his wife’s maid. If you were to look at that page, truly, I believe even the devil would feel ashamed. The things written on that page, the nature of the criticism, the foul language directed at ministers... and if all of that is deemed acceptable, then how can we stand here and put the entire blame solely on the media?” she said. Social media is used for mud-slinging, and political parties are also responsible, she said. “Those who have turned into mobile and Facebook media stoop to slandering anyone’s character whenever they wish, taking less than two minutes to demean someone’s dignity. And in this, if anyone is most responsible, it is the political parties,” she added. She also referred to the pages run by political parties. “You will see how an individual’s dignity is shredded to pieces. There is zero regulation over it. And yet you say our brothers in the media are in the wrong. They may be wrong as well; I do not deny that, because nowadays genuine, accredited media persons are few, while the number of self-styled Facebook media pages is huge,” she said. The Minister suggested that members and journalists should not be allowed to keep mobile phones inside the House. She assured the House that the Information Department will introduce a comprehensive policy with rules, regulations and proper scrutiny. “Following that, if anyone is found guilty of malpractice, strict action must be taken against them,” she said. title: 20 African wild dogs were brought back to a Zimbabwe park after disappearing for decades; conservationists rebuilt the ecosystem before their return
original_content: African wild dogs returned to Zimbabwe’s Matusadona National Park in February 2026 after disappearing from the area for decades. 20 animals were moved into the park in two established packs, marking a major step in the restoration of a predator that had been locally extinct there. But the return did not begin with the release itself. African Parks and the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority had spent years rebuilding protection, wildlife populations, monitoring systems and community links across Matusadona before the dogs arrived. How 20 African wild dogs returned to Matusadona after decades The 20 African wild dogs were translocated between 15 and 17 February 2026, according to African Parks. The animals came from Nuanetsi Ranch in southern Zimbabwe and were moved in 2 established packs, with 6 dogs in one and 14 in the other. The operation was led by African Parks and the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority, or ZimParks. NineDaysinEden reported that the process involved wildlife specialists, veterinarians, aircraft crews and conservation teams, with the animals undergoing health checks and careful monitoring before transport. The dogs were not released straight into the wider park. Instead, they were placed in specially built holding facilities near Tashinga for several weeks. This soft-release approach gave the packs time to recover from the journey, become familiar with their surroundings, maintain their social bonds and begin establishing a connection with the new territory. African wild dog pack. Image Credit: Wikipedia Matusadona was rebuilt before these predators arrived The return of the dogs followed 5 years of conservation work in the park. African Parks said its partnership with ZimParks was formalised in 2020, after which efforts focused on strengthening anti-poaching systems, ranger training, biodiversity monitoring, infrastructure and community programmes. Wildlife restoration was also part of that work. According to African Parks, zebra, buffalo, sable and eland had been moved into the park as part of efforts to rebuild its wildlife populations and restore the wider ecosystem. This preparation mattered because wild dogs need more than a protected patch of land. SafariFind reported that the species generally requires large, connected landscapes with enough prey and relatively low levels of direct persecution. Packs can travel beyond park boundaries, making cooperation with neighbouring communities and land managers important to their survival. Importance of wild dogs to the restored ecosystem African wild dogs are among Africa’s most endangered large carnivores. African Parks puts the number remaining in the wild at fewer than 7,000, while its detailed species information gives an approximate figure of 6,600. Their importance is not limited to being a rare wildlife sighting. They are highly social predators that hunt cooperatively and help regulate prey populations. The African Bush Camps Foundation said their return contributes to restoring the ecological balance of Matusadona. The species faces several threats across Zimbabwe and elsewhere. SafariFind identifies habitat fragmentation, snares, disease, conflict with people, road deaths and declining prey as continuing pressures. Wild dogs can also travel through communal areas and private land, meaning conservation efforts cannot stop at the boundaries of a national park. GPS tracking will help keep the packs safe The newly introduced dogs are being closely watched as they settle into Matusadona. African Parks reported that all adult wild dogs were fitted with GPS collars so their movements and social behaviour can be followed. The park has also introduced a GPS-based geofence warning system around nearby settlements. When collared wildlife approaches these areas, alerts can be triggered so conservation teams can respond before animals move into inhabited locations. African Parks reported that 12 rangers from Nyaminyami Rural District Council have been brought into the park’s operational structure, while 8 Human-Wildlife Conflict Ward Monitors are working in important areas of neighbouring chiefdoms. The monitors provide an early-warning link between communities and park authorities and can report incidents quickly. The return forms part of a wider recovery Matusadona covers 1,470 square kilometres along the southern shores of Lake Kariba, according to African Parks. Its habitats include floodplains, the drowned forest and the Zambezi Escarpment, supporting animals such as elephants, buffalo, lions and leopards as well as more than 240 bird species. The wild dogs are therefore returning to a landscape where broader restoration work is already under way. African Parks said their reintroduction also supports conservation across the wider Sebungwe region. SafariFind estimates about 660 wild dogs in 86 packs across the country, although it notes that figures vary according to surveys and sources. Important populations remain in the Greater Hwange Ecosystem, the Zambezi Valley and the south-east lowveld. The long-term outcome for the Matusadona packs will depend on what happens after their release. African Parks said the team will continue tracking their movements, social dynamics and adaptation, with the information helping in future management.

The dogs were moved in two packs from Nuanetsi Ranch and placed in holding facilities for several weeks before release. This followed five years of conservation efforts to rebuild wildlife populations, infrastructure, and community relations. GPS collars will track the dogs' movements to ensure their safety and adaptation.

title: Sivakasi fireworks industry upbeat as Supreme Court permits manufacture of joined green crackers
original_content: Fireworks manufacturers in Sivakasi are jubilant over the Supreme Court passing an order on Wednesday (September 30, 2026), permitting them to manufacture next-generation joined green crackers. “This is a significant milestone for the fireworks industry and a great day for all stakeholders,” said P. Ganesan, an office-bearer of the Tamil Nadu Fireworks and Amorces Manufacturers’ Association, Sivakasi. The Supreme Court has laid down a few conditions for making chorsa, and the details of those conditions are awaited. “The basic condition is that joined crackers should be made using only green crackers,” he added. The industry has been fighting it out legally in the Supreme Court, seeking to lift the ban on chorsa, one of the most popular products in the fireworks industry, since 2018. Major manufacturers’ bodies like TANFAMA and The Indian Fireworks Manufacturers’ Association (TIFMA) had impleaded themselves in the case. TIFMA general secretary, T. Kannan, said the Supreme Court order lifting the ban on chorsa will have a significant impact on the future course of the industry, as joined crackers form 20% of the total production of fireworks goods. With the ban on chorsa, many manufacturers, both big and small, rushed to making aerial crackers that required a lot of expertise, and it led to an increased number of accidents, he said. “Now, the industry can relax a bit and many could resume making chorsa, which has a good market,” he added. Chorsa comes in different variants, from those having small single-shot crackers (bijli) numbering from 28 to 10,000. “This is one of the most affordable products in the fireworks industry and people from across all economic strata could buy it,” Mr. Ganesan said. Though the manufacturers could attempt to make available joined crackers of different sizes and numbers during the ensuing Deepavali, its mass production could be possible only for the next festival season, they say. “We have been left with only one month for Deepavali. With the State and Central government officials already having intensified the inspection of fireworks units for implementation of safety procedures, manufacturing chorsa on a mass scale in a short time is not possible,” said Mr. Ganesan. title: Techie Kavin caste killing case: Madras High Court quashes charge sheet against parents of prime accused Surjith
original_content: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), quashed the charge sheet filed by the CB-CID against Saravanan and Krishnakumari, parents of Surjith, who is the main accused in the Kavin Selvaganesh caste killing case. Kavin, who belonged to a Scheduled Caste and hailed from Arumugamangalam near Eral in Thoothukudi district, was in a relationship with S. Subhashini of Palayamkottai, a Siddha doctor. Kavin was murdered on July 27, 2025 in Tirunelveli. Surjith, Subhashini’s younger brother, was arrested on charges of murder. Later, his cousin Jayapal and his parents were arraigned as co-accused in the case. Under suspension The charge sheet filed against Saravanan and Krishnakumari — both police sub-inspectors now placed under suspension — before the II Additional District Court (PCR Act Cases), Tirunelveli, said they had learnt about the relationship between Kavin and their daughter in 2016-17. Thereafter, Saravanan cautioned his daughter and spoke to Kavin over phone during 2018-19. Besides, Krishnakumari had contacted Kavin’s mother over phone, informed her about the relationship and warned her. On July 27, 2025, Surjith had informed his father about Kavin’s murder and the latter also informed his wife Krishnakumari. The police’s final report said they met Surjith near a college and instructed him to destroy his clothes and mobile phone, and remove the number plate of the two-wheeler. Saravanan had also furnished false information to the police. Grounds for quashing charge sheet However, Justice R. Vijayakumar said there was no eyewitness to the meeting. There was no CCTV camera footage, photograph, video recording, or statement of any independent witness. There was no recording, transcript, message, or any other electronic material disclosing what transpired between them, the judge added. “The meeting is sought to be established solely on the circumstance that the mobile phones attributed to Surjith, Saravanan, and Krishnakumari, were connected to the same mobile tower during the relevant period,” the judge observed. Relying on a Supreme Court verdict, the judge said mobile tower information corresponds only to the operational range of the tower and not to the exact location of the mobile phone. It would, therefore, be unsafe to rely solely upon such material to prove the presence of an accused at a particular place. “It is the prosecution’s own case, as recorded in the final report, that Saravanan proceeded to the scene of occurrence within 16 minutes of receiving information from Surjith and spoke to the police there. It is also the prosecution’s case that he informed a head constable that the murder had been committed by his son. Where the prosecution’s own material shows that the person accused of screening had, within minutes, gone to the police and named the offender as his own son, the very intention which forms the essential ingredient of the offences stands negatived by the prosecution’s own narrative. The two versions cannot co-exist,” the judge held. Referring to telephone conversions, the court said, the ingredient of caste reference, insult, or abuse and the ingredient of public view are conspicuously absent. The telephonic communications relied upon took place several years before the occurrence. The foundational requirements for invoking the relevant Sections under the SC/ST Act are absent. Plea of Surjith’s cousin dismissed However, the court dismissed a petition filed by Surjith’s cousin Jayapal, a co-accused in whose quarry premises, Surjith is believed to have destroyed his clothes, mobile phone and the number plate of a two-wheeler soon after Kavin was murdered. The court said whether Jayapal had a plan or was party to a conspiracy in the murder committed by Surjith is a question that must abide the trial and cannot be gone into at the stage of a quash petition. T.N. government must raise appeal: Thirumavalavan In a statement, VCK president Thol. Thirumavalavan, on Tuesday, urged the Tamil Nadu government to appeal against the quashing of the charge sheet and said the court’s move had set a “wrong precedent”. In a statement, he said: “While it is within the court’s authority to acquit someone in a case for lack of evidence, the court’s decision to quash the charge sheet even before the commencement of the trial would set a “wrong precedent.” “It is worth noting that Saravanan, arrested in this case, was released on bail only to be rearrested for his alleged links to a gang of contract killers in yet another murder case. The High Court’s action has created an impression that such an individual and his wife are innocent,” he said. Published - September 30, 2026 12:40 am IST

The court dismissed Jayapal’s plea but urged the Tamil Nadu government to appeal, citing insufficient evidence linking Saravanan and Krishnakumari to shielding their son from charges.

title: Explained: How US Controls Iraq's Oil Revenues
original_content: US forces are set to withdraw on Wednesday from their last bases in Iraq, a departure celebrated as a victory by Iran and its allies, which have deep influence in the country where 4,500 Americans died during more than two decades of war. Still, since its 2003 invasion of Iraq, the US has held effective control of the country's oil revenue dollars, giving Washington extraordinary leverage over Baghdad's affairs, with implications for regional dynamics involving Iran. How Does The US Control Iraq's Oil Revenues? This stems primarily from the management of Iraq's oil income through the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. After the 2003 invasion, the Coalition Provisional Authority (CPA), led by the US, set up the Development Fund for Iraq (DFI), held at the New York Fed, and designed to collect the oil revenues for use in reconstruction and development efforts. The Fund also aimed to protect the Iraqi oil revenues from lawsuits and claims relating to Saddam Hussein's rule. An executive order by then president George W. Bush to set up the arrangement has been renewed by every president since. The DFI eventually became an account of the Central Bank of Iraq at the New York Federal Reserve, as it remains today. What Leverage Does This Give The US Over Iraq? Oil is Iraq's most important revenue source, making up about 90% of the state budget. This gives Washington significant sway over the country's economic and political stability. When the Iraqi government asked US troops to leave in 2020, Washington reportedly threatened to cut Iraq's access to the New York Federal Reserve funds, with Baghdad ultimately backing down. While Iraq has gained more control over its financial affairs since the early years of the occupation, the link highlights the enduring influence of the US on the economic landscape of Iraq, even as the latter seeks to assert sovereignty and independence. Why Has The Arrangement Endured For So Long? The system helped anchor Iraq's financial stability and safeguards state finances, government officials told Reuters on condition of anonymity. It boosts international confidence in the management of oil income, eases access to US dollars needed for trade and imports, and protects revenues from external claims and financial shocks, including claims by creditors and lawsuits, they said. The arrangement supports exchange-rate stability and underpins confidence in the Iraqi economy, while working to strengthen domestic financial institutions and assert greater economic sovereignty, they added. It also allows the government to push back against some actors, such as Iran-allied groups, who seek fewer curbs on dollar access. Last year, the US imposed sanctions on Iraqi banks and individuals it accused of laundering money for Iran. How Has This Arrangement Affected Iraq? The heavy curbs on US dollar supply led to a parallel, informal market for dollars, resulting in a price spread between the official exchange rate set by the central bank and that on the black market. The price difference is essentially a risk premium for dealing outside the formal system. In his second term, President Donald Trump has pursued a campaign of maximum pressure on Iran, with Iraq often caught in the crossfire as Tehran has used it as a vital economic lung. The war he launched with Israel against Iran on February 28 added further pressure on Baghdad. What Is The Status Of Iraq's Oil Revenue Management? Iraqi oil revenues remain in the custody of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. CBI has historically used dollar auctions, formally known as the foreign currency window, as the main mechanism to supply dollars. Private banks and exchange houses could bid daily to purchase US dollars using Iraqi dinars. Iraq formally ended the auction system at the start of 2025 after significant US pressure, part of a broad crackdown on alleged siphoning of dollars to sanctioned parties, especially Iran. This arrangement continues to influence regional dynamics involving Iran.

title: Jiya Joshi was rejected from volunteering at a nursing home at 14; she later built a lifesaving 500-student senior care movement
original_content: Jiya Joshi lost her beloved grandmother at 14 and decided to volunteer at a nursing home. But getting rejected from there inspired her to begin a movement uniting generations through friendship, compassion and caring. A love lost too soon Jiya was only two when her grandparents arrived from India to Texas, to help care for her while her parents were at work. Her grandmother, Saroj, drove her to school and cooked her the most delicious snacks. Her entire day was wrapped around them and the two formed a close bond, sharing long conversations about life, school and friends. When she was in third grade, her grandparents returned to India, but distance only made the heart grow fonder, and they spoke on the phone regularly once a week. The year she turned 14, Jiya lost her grandmother, whom she called 'Dadi' and the loss left an aching void inside her, often leaving her feeling lonely. While she had her parents and friends to talk to, it wasn't the same. They didn't carry the same wisdom and gentle kindness as her grandmother did. Filling the void Within two years of service, Jiya has helped 4,000 seniors, built a network of more than 70 youth volunteers and spread the initiative in more than 11 countries through an ambassador program. This is when an idea struck. “What if I visit a nursing home? Maybe the residents would enjoy a visit as much as I would?” she asked. Jiya decided to volunteer at a nursing home and after being put on hold several times, she finally reached the nursing home volunteer coordinator: "I want to volunteer and visit," she explained, as per a report by Woman's World. The administrator was welcoming until she learnt Jiya was only 14. “We don’t allow volunteers under 18,” she declared. “Our staff doesn’t have time to care for both children and our seniors.” Jiya's heart was crushed, and not just due to the rejection. There was also the lingering grief of having lost one of her favourite people in the world, her Dadi. After several more refusals to volunteer, she decided to do something different. “Could I come just once — a trial visit?” she asked Sharon Williams, Activities Director at Houston’s Landon Ridge Assisted Living. “If it doesn’t work, I won’t bother you again.” Williams was touched by the girl's sincerity and decided to agree. "Let's give it a try," she said and Jiya was over the moon. Jiya arrived for her first visit at the centre with a box of supplies. She approached a group of seniors in a recreation area, put on a bright smile and introduced herself. “I’m Jiya. Would you like to paint with me?” “I love painting!” exclaimed a woman named Betty and soon she was regaling Jiya with incredible tales of her years as a nurse in Vietnam. “I was a pilot fighting the Germans in World War II,” said a second resident, and a third rushed off and returned with a chunk of concrete. “You mentioned Germany; this is part of the Berlin Wall, a piece of history,” she explained. As the word of a youthful stranger spread, residents who rarely left their rooms came out to see what the excitement was about. By the end of her visit, Jiya had made a dozen new friends and spread even more smiles. “I’ve never seen them so active,” Sharon marvelled as she helped Jiya pack up. “You’re coming back, right?” Jiya returned every Saturday that summer. While the residents loved having such a lively young person around to hold conversation and company with, Jiya loved their stories and affectionate hugs. A generational movement When school started again, Jiya invited her friends to join her and many of them said yes. The teens visited in pairs and after a few outings, many told Jiya, "This is the most fun I've had volunteering." It was one invitation from Betty that caught her by surprise. "Betty asked me to keep her company at the senior home’s 4th of July event because she did not have any family to eat with her at the event," Jiya shared. This is when she thought about how many seniors were in need of active company. Roughly one in four Americans aged 65 and older is socially isolated, and 30–35% of seniors report feeling lonely at least some of the time. This isolation is linked to serious health risks, including higher rates of depression, heart disease, stroke, and cognitive decline. As interest spread, Jiya founded a youth-led non-profit organisation, Young and Old United, a movement that allowed teens to volunteer at elder care facilities while spreading love and support among hundreds of seniors across Houston. Generations were united through the feelings of friendship, compassion and care. Within two years of service, Jiya has helped 4,000 seniors, built a network of more than 70 youth volunteers and spread the initiative in more than 11 countries through an ambassador program. Together, they have raised $9,000 through local fundraisers and grants and partnered with dentists to obtain dental kits to include in hygiene kits. Hundreds of middle and high school students have begun making regular nursing home visits across the state. She mobilises youth volunteers to assemble and personally deliver hygiene kits to isolated and underrepresented seniors, offer spa days to senior women, and conduct senior interviews. YOU has also won thousands of dollars in grants from Youth Service America, AmeriCorps, and H.E.B and has an ongoing partnership with staff from United Airlines, providing hygiene kits. “Their eyes light up when they see her coming,” said Sharon. "My grandmother was a bright personality. She was a safe space where I could talk about anything. Then, when she left my life, I sought to regain the strongest connection I had ever built by reaching out to seniors within my own neighbourhood," Jiya told Bold Journey. “Our seniors still have so much to offer,” Jiya insists. “My grandmother taught me that. I can feel her smiling down on me!” Jiya hopes to help more than 3000+ seniors in 2026.
prev_rephrased: **Jiya Joshi**, inspired by the loss of her grandmother at 14, tried to volunteer at a nursing home but was rejected due to age. Undeterred, she convinced **Sharon Williams** to let her visit once and ended up founding **Young and Old United**, which has helped over 4,000 seniors, built a network of more than 70 youth volunteers, and spread to 11 countries, raising $9,000 in grants.

title: When caste pride slays young love
original_content: The quiet hamlet of Arumugamangalam near the banks of the Tamirabharani in southern Tamil Nadu’s Thoothukudi district has just about 300 families. Since Sunday last (July 27), however, the residents have lost sleep, with senior Ministers, politicians, top police officers, and leaders of caste outfits visiting this otherwise nondescript village. This would mark the Indian central bank's first meeting after the US Federal Reserve increased rates earlier this month.
