These residents lack formal ownership rights and face difficulties repairing their homes. The NGO seeks a permanent solution including excising civilian pockets from cantonment limits, granting absolute freehold ownership, converting remaining defence land into exclusive military stations, and improving civic amenities. Published September 30, 2026.

title: ₹3,000 crore drugs seized from Iranian boat in Arabian Sea; 5 Pakistan nationals detained
original_content: The Indian Coast Guard, in a joint operation with the Gujarat ATS, has seized 526 kg of methamphetamine and heroin valued at more than ₹3,000 crore from an Iranian boat in the Arabian Sea, officials said on Wednesday (September 30, 2026). Five Pakistani nationals operating the vessel were also detained in the operation carried out near Lakshadweep on September 25, the Coast Guard said in a statement. Based on intelligence inputs, Coast Guard assets carried out sea-air surveillance and tracked the suspicious dhow before launching a hot pursuit and boarding it west of Lakshadweep, it said. The seized contraband comprised high-grade methamphetamine and heroin, the Coast Guard said. The vessel, its crew and the seized drugs were brought to Mumbai under armed escort for joint interrogation and further legal proceedings, it said. The operation was conducted in coordination with the Gujarat Anti-Terrorist Squad. The State ATS also confirmed the apprehension of five Pakistani nationals. It is scheduled to brief the media on the operation later in the day. The seizure comes as security agencies step up efforts to curb transnational drug trafficking through the maritime route. The Coast Guard said the operation demonstrated its surveillance and maritime interdiction capabilities and its commitment to preventing illicit activities in India's maritime zones. The seizure would help disrupt the financial network of international drug syndicates and prevent synthetic drugs from reaching the mainland, it added. ‘Determined to shiled youth’ Union Home Minister Amit Shah praised the joint operation and said that the “Modi government is determined to shield its youth from the scourge of drugs”. In a post on X, Mr. Shah lauded the Coast Guard, Gujarat ATS, and central agencies for ‘upholding a stellar example of coordination and cooperation’. (with PTI inputs) Published - September 30, 2026 09:14 am IST

title: Accept voter documents on WhatsApp, verify at homes if needed: Maharashtra poll body to BLOs
original_content: Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer S. Chockalingam has asked poll officials to take into consideration voter documents sent via WhatsApp during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, and has directed Booth Level Officers (BLOs) to visit households for verification if necessary, an official said on Wednesday (September 30, 2026). People can respond to notices generated from the ECINet software by sending the required documents on WhatsApp to BLOs, the official in the State poll body said. "The BLOs have been asked to visit homes for verification of the documents sent, if required," he said. Officials earlier said Mr. Chockalingam had requested the Election Commission for changes in the ECINet software to allow Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to use their discretion regarding anomalies in electoral rolls. The Opposition Congress has, however, alleged that the statutory powers of EROs to decide voter eligibility were being diluted through the ECINet system. The deadline for filing claims and objections for the SIR of electoral rolls in Maharashtra has been extended from Wednesday (September 30, 2026) to October 12, 2026. The period for disposal of notices, and of claims and objections, is until November 10, 2026, and the date for final publication is November 16, 2026. The Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar have come under fire after it came to light that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months to decisions and orders regarding the SIR, some of which they said were issued without their knowledge. The Opposition parties have accused Mr. Kumar of taking unilateral decisions in favour of the ruling establishment. The Election Commission has clarified in a statement that the three-member Commission took decisions, including those relating to the SIR of electoral rolls, unanimously. title: Centre notifies new CAFE norms, tightens fuel-efficiency targets for passenger vehicles
original_content: The Centre has notified the new Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE-3) norms that set carbon emission limits for passenger vehicles. The norms will take effect from April 1, 2027, and remain in force until March 31, 2032 Under the new norms, the fuel-consumption benchmark will be tightened from 3.996 litres per 100 km in 2027–28 to 3.3273 litres per 100 km in 2031–32, amounting to an improvement of about 16.7% over the five-year period. The new rules will apply to new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. The new Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency framework will have targets tightening year-on-year across all five years. “The revised target line has also been flattened to provide a more balanced, weight sensitive approach, with relatively softer targets for lighter vehicles and greater fuel efficiency requirements for heavier vehicles,” according to the Ministry of Power. The reference weight has been raised from 1,082 kg under the existing norms to 1,229 kg under the new framework, which is an increase of around 13.6 per cent, reflecting the shift towards heavier vehicles in the passenger car segment. The norms also offer manufacturers a range of incentives and compliance pathways to encourage the adoption of cleaner fuels, technologies and more efficient vehicles. The framework recognises the role of renewable and low-carbon fuels, including ethanol-blended petrol, biofuels and compressed biogas (CBG), through the introduction of a Carbon Neutrality Factor (CNF). Under the framework, manufacturers can avail of a concession of 1 g CO₂/km for each eligible technology, subject to an overall cap of 9.0 g Published - September 30, 2026 11:48 am IST

title: Ex-IAS officer found dead at home in Bhopal
original_content: A 70-year-old retired IAS officer, Rakesh Agarwal, was found dead with his throat slit at his home in Bhopal on Wednesday (September 30, 2026), police said. title: Who is attending INDIA Bloc meet today? Mamata Banerjee, other top leaders gather in Delhi over EC row
original_content: Top leaders of the INDIA bloc are meeting in the national capital on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) to discuss pressing issues, particularly focusing on irregularities surrounding the SIR exercise, and to finalise a high-stakes action plan for a nationwide joint agitation against the Election Commission (EC). Also read: INDIA bloc meeting LIVE updates Fight for CEC’s resignation The primary agenda of the meeting is to finalise an action plan for a joint protest against the EC, specifically targeting the alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise and pushing for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. A draft notice has been prepared to introduce a motion both in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha for the CEC’s removal and various leaders are expected to contribute suggestions during the deliberations. Key leaders attending the high-stakes meet Several key leaders and the Congress party leadership met in New Delhi on September 30. Key participants include Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former party chief Rahul Gandhi, AICC general secretaries Jairam Ramesh and K. C. Venugopal, along with TMC leaders Mamata Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee. Leaders from various parties such as the SP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP(SP) and Shiv Sena (UBT) are also in attendance. Which allies are skipping INDIA bloc meeting Some notable allies did not participate in the meeting. Both the DMK and AAP did not attend, citing differing reasons. Moreover, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is not present due to nominations for Rajya Sabha polls in UP, though he has sent representatives in his stead. Asked about Mr. Yadav not coming to the meeting, Mr. Venugpal said, “I spoke to Akhilesh Yadav, Congress president Malikarjun Kharge also spoke to him. He has Rajya Sabha election nominations to take care of but his party leaders are attending.” Asked whether attempts would be made to get parties like the DMK and AAP on board, Mr. Venugopal said those types of issues would be discussed. “The DMK was very much part of INDIA bloc. Still we believe they are all against this type of attack on democracy. That is our thinking, let us see,” he added. On the INDIA bloc meeting, DMK spokesperson T.K.S. Elangovan said, “Ideologically, we all stand together. Maybe we are not part of the INDIA alliance. That is different. But in Parliament, we will support whoever brings a removal motion against Gyanesh Kumar... our leader had issued a statement. On many of the issues where other opposition parties oppose the BJP, we will also stand by them. That doesn’t mean that we are together. We are not in the INDIA bloc.” The issue of alleged irregularities in the SIR is being seen by the opposition INDIA bloc as an opportunity to close ranks and corner the government. The meeting comes days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders on the SIR (Special Intensive Revision) that they said were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.
